national_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of the labour force in Bosnia and Herzegovina aged 15 to 74 who are unemployed for 12 months or more. The labour force comprises employed and unemployed persons. Unemployed persons are defined as persons aged 15 to 74 who were without work during the reference week, were available to start work within the following two weeks, and had either actively sought work during the previous four weeks or had already found a job to start within the following three months. The duration of unemployment is defined as the duration of job search or, if shorter, the time elapsed since the last employment. The definitions and methodological approach are aligned with the methodology of the European Union and the standards of the International Labour Organization.
national_rationale: The indicator is used to monitor long-term unemployment and labour-market conditions in Bosnia and Herzegovina within Sustainable Development Goal 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth. Monitoring long-term unemployment provides insight into the situation of people who remain unemployed for an extended period and supports the monitoring of changes in opportunities to participate in the labour market. Reducing long-term unemployment contributes to higher employment, activation of the labour force and improved conditions for decent and sustainable work.
national_methodology_characteristics: The indicator monitors the long-term unemployment rate among the labour force in Bosnia and Herzegovina aged 15 to 74. A lower value indicates a favourable development of the indicator. Data are monitored in accordance with the EU methodology for this indicator, enabling comparable monitoring of trends in long-term unemployment. Changes in the indicator are used to monitor long-term labour-market developments and progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals.
national_long_objective: Long-term reduction of the long-term unemployment rate in Bosnia and Herzegovina, accompanied by increased employment opportunities, activation of unemployed persons and the creation of conditions for sustainable and decent employment.
eu_indicator_definition: The indicator measures the share of the labour force aged 15 to 74 who are unemployed for 12 months or more. The labour force comprises employed and unemployed persons. Unemployed persons are defined as persons aged 15 to 74 who were without work during the reference week, were available to start work within the following two weeks, and had either actively sought work during the previous four weeks or had already found a job to start within the following three months. The duration of unemployment is defined as the duration of job search or, if shorter, the time elapsed since the last employment.
eu_rationale: The indicator is used to monitor long-term unemployment and progress towards Sustainable Development Goal 8 – Decent Work and Economic Growth. Within the European Pillar of Social Rights, the indicator contributes to monitoring labour market functioning and the situation of people experiencing prolonged unemployment. Reducing long-term unemployment is associated with improving access to employment, activating unemployed persons and creating better conditions for decent work.
eu_methodology_characteristics: The indicator monitors changes in the long-term unemployment rate among the labour force aged 15 to 74. A lower value indicates a favourable development of the indicator. In the EU, the long-term unemployment rate decreased from 2.7% in 2019 to 1.9% in 2025, indicating a long-term reduction in long-term unemployment. The indicator is used to monitor progress in employment and labour-market conditions in the context of Sustainable Development Goal 8 and the European Pillar of Social Rights.
eu_long_objective: Long-term reduction of the long-term unemployment rate, accompanied by increased employment opportunities, activation of unemployed persons and improved conditions for sustainable and decent employment.
